subject: DPA: incident notice windows & cross-border forensic handoff (action items)
content:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA: incident notice windows & cross-border forensic handoff (action items)

Hi Elena —

Following our contract review: we want to align on the incident-notice and evidence-handover language in the DPA so both teams have a clear, operational workflow. High-level asks:

- Confirm whether FinBridge can accept a 24-hour customer notification window for confirmed incidents (Redwood will send an initial notice with scope and impact).
- Clarify whether FinBridge will accept encrypted forensic exports to a Redwood-managed SFTP in the EU (if data subject is EU) or whether you require evidence to remain on your side.
- If cross-border exports are restricted, please confirm acceptable handoff mechanisms (forensic agent, remote screen share, onsite transfer) and expected timelines.

I've sketched a draft clause to make this concrete and attached it (proposed_dpa_incident_clause_v1.docx). Kimberly / Ben — can you review the attachment and flag any operational blockers?

Goal: agree on minimal notice windows + one of three evidence handover options so we can ship a DPA amendment before EOY.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Head of Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

---

From: Elena Rossi <elena@finbridge.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: FinBridge Security Ops <secops@finbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 11:34:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notice windows & cross-border forensic handoff (action items)

Aisha —

Thanks for laying this out. A few immediate clarifications from FinBridge: 

- Notification windows: we can commit to confirming a verified breach within 48 hours of detection for incidents that materially affect customer data. For lower-severity events we typically acknowledge within 72 hours. A 24-hour confirmed notice is aggressive for us unless there is a clear automated detection feed.

- Forensic exports: FinBridge cannot permit raw forensic exports containing EU personal data to be transferred outside the EEA without an executed DPA amendment and appropriate transfer mechanism (SCCs/adequate safeguards).

- Acceptable handoff options: (1) Secure SFTP endpoint hosted in the EEA with encrypted bundles and access logs; (2) Remote forensic session with FinBridge analysts that extracts agreed artifacts (we can provide a forensics playbook fragment); (3) Limited onsite evidence transfer under NDAs/escrow when legally required.

If Redwood can accept a 48-hour initial confirmation and commit to the EU-hosted SFTP + audit logs model (or agree to remote sessions), we can sign an amendment faster. I'll ask SecOps to produce a short import/export checklist to attach.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
VP, Security & Privacy
FinBridge

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@finbridge.com>, FinBridge Security Ops <secops@finbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notice windows & cross-border forensic handoff (action items)

Thanks Elena — that helps. Quick internal notes and a suggested compromise clause (attached):

- Operational assumption: detection feeds will vary by customer integration. Redwood can commit to an initial "customer-impact" notification within 24 hours for high-severity incidents we detect and verify; for incidents where additional triage is required, we propose a 48-hour confirmation window. We should keep that conditional in the clause.

- Evidence handover: propose a three-path approach in the DPA: 
  * Path A (preferred): Encrypted SFTP in the EEA — Redwood requests an encrypted bundle and access to logs; FinBridge retains control; transfer initiated within 72 hours of formal request.
  * Path B: Remote forensic session — FinBridge provides controlled extraction with live screen/video and artifact handoff; session scheduled within 72 hours.
  * Path C: Escrow/onsite transfer — only if legally requested; timeline negotiated but treated as expedited.

- Export controls: all exports containing EU personal data must be packaged with minimal necessary fields and pseudonymized where possible. Agree on export format and a whitelist of artifact types (memory image, logs with timestamps, application-level events).

I've attached the proposed wording: proposed_dpa_incident_clause_v1.docx — it includes conditional notice language, a table of timelines, and a short artifact whitelist. Ben — can you confirm whether the 72-hour extraction window is realistic from a cost/SLA perspective?

Kimberly Park
Sr. Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_dpa_incident_clause_v1.docx (Draft clause + timelines table)

---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finbridge.com>, FinBridge Security Ops <secops@finbridge.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notice windows & cross-border forensic handoff (action items)

Elena / SecOps —

Appreciate the quick reply. To keep momentum before EOY: Redwood can accept the following compromise for the amendment we will circulate for signature: 

1) Notification: Redwood will send an initial incident notice within 24 hours for high-severity confirmed incidents, and a conditional confirmation within 48 hours where further triage is needed.

2) Evidence / exports: For EU personal data, FinBridge will provide either (i) encrypted forensic bundles to an EEA-hosted SFTP managed by FinBridge with audit logs and a time-limited access token for Redwood; or (ii) a remotely-run, recorded forensic extraction session with FinBridge analysts. Redwood will request minimal necessary artifacts; items and formats will follow the attached whitelist.

3) Timeline: Metadata and scope provided within 48 hours; artifact transfer (per chosen Path A or B) initiated within 72 hours after formal request. Full raw forensic images only on lawful request and with executed amendment (and/or approved SCCs).

4) Export controls: All exports will be encrypted in transit and at rest; pseudonymization applied where feasible. Parties will log transfers and retain access logs for 12 months.

Elena — can you confirm by EOD Tue 22 Dec whether FinBridge will accept the EEA-hosted SFTP option or prefers the remote session as the default? If yes, we'll circulate a focused DPA amendment and a short checklist (Ben / Kimberly to review).

Thanks — looping Legal Ops to start the amendment paperwork once you confirm.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
